# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

# [tinydb] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:462522e69b6b⟧
Mode: Code Development (code)

Legend: 🎯session ●bugfix ◆feature ↻refactor ✓change ○discovery ⚖decision ⚠security_alert ⚷security_note ⊘sensitive
Format: ID TIME TYPE TITLE
Fetch details: get_observations([IDs]) | Search: mem-search skill

Stats: 13 obs (4,015t read) | 87,840t work | 95% savings

### Nov 4, 2026
1 12:59a ○ Table reads go through _read_table, which delegates to storage.read on each access
2 " ○ _read_table re-reads storage on every call, and search cache shares mutable document objects
3 1:00a ◆ Added scripts/bench_read.py to benchmark TinyDB read paths on a large JSON database
4 " ○ Parsing the JSON file dominates TinyDB read latency on a 44MB database
5 " ○ cProfile shows db.all() cost splits between JSON decoding and per-document Document construction
S2 Benchmark TinyDB read performance on a ~40MB JSON database, add a benchmark script under scripts/, and explain where the time goes. Follow-up: commit the benchmark and discuss cache invalidation options for a JSONStorage parse cache. (Nov 4, 1:00 AM)
S1 Benchmark TinyDB read performance on a ~40MB JSON database: test whether JSONStorage re-parses the whole file per query, add a benchmark script under scripts/, and report where the time goes. (Nov 4, 1:00 AM)
6 " ✓ Committed scripts/bench_read.py as 4cfb380 with a read-performance benchmark message
7 1:03a ○ JSONStorage keeps one open file handle and re-parses it fully on every read
8 " ○ Table writes are full-database read-modify-write cycles through a single JSON handle
9 1:04a ◆ JSONStorage now caches parsed data keyed on file inode, size, mtime, and ctime
10 " ✓ Table._update_table invalidates the storage parse cache when an updater raises
11 " ○ Parse cache verified: 3 reads cost one parse, and external rewrites are picked up including same-mtime rewrites
12 " ○ Test suite cannot start: pytest.ini passes coverage flags that the environment's pytest does not accept
13 " ○ Full test suite passes (228 tests) with the parse cache; benchmark shows db.all and uncached search dropped substantially
S3 Continue read-performance work on TinyDB: repeated reads should not re-parse the JSON file when it is unchanged, while edits from the external importer must still be visible. (Nov 4, 1:04 AM)
**Investigated**: Traced the read and write paths in tinydb/storages.py and tinydb/table.py: JSONStorage keeps one open handle, read() re-parses the whole file on each call, _read_table() and _update_table() each call storage.read(), and writes go through the same handle. Ran the 40 MB benchmark and the full test suite with pytest.ini bypassed. A standalone check script (/tmp/t_cache.py) exercised cache hits, external rewrites, mtime-preserving rewrites, and a failing updater. The initial pytest run failed because pytest.ini passes coverage flags that the installed pytest does not accept.

**Learned**: JSONStorage.read() re-parsed the full file on every call, which made each uncached search almost entirely parse time. A parse cache keyed on inode, size, mtime, and ctime detects external rewrites, including ones that restore the old mtime, because ctime still changes. Files modified within the last 2 seconds are not cached, which guards against timestamp-granularity races. The cached object is shared with callers, and an updater that fails partway can leave the cache partially modified unless invalidated. Document construction in db.all() is unaffected by the parse cache.

**Completed**: Added a parse cache to JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py, with a signature check, a 2-second settle window, invalidation in write() and close(), and a public invalidate_cache() method. Added cache invalidation in Table._update_table() in tinydb/table.py when an updater raises. The 228-test suite passes with pytest.ini bypassed. The benchmark shows an uncached search dropping from about 465 ms to about 39 ms and db.all() from about 822 ms to a median of about 313 ms on the synthetic 43.9 MB database. The changes are not committed, and no new tests have been added.

**Next Steps**: The session is at a checkpoint. The open questions are whether to commit the cache changes and whether to add tests for the invalidation cases: external in-place rewrite, mtime-preserving rewrite, failed updater, and the settle window. The pytest.ini coverage-flag problem still needs a fix for the normal test command.

**Notes**: Two caveats remain. Cached read() results are shared objects, so mutating nested values in a returned document would corrupt later reads. If the importer replaces the file by rename rather than rewriting it in place, the open handle keeps pointing at the old inode, so read() would need to stat the path and reopen. Both caveats predate this change except that the cache makes the shared-object issue more consequential. The benchmark and test results come from one machine and one run.
